title: When Occupation-derived Skills Don't Help: On the Limits of Skill-Augmented Career Path Prediction
abstract: arXiv:2610.20186v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Skills are widely assumed to play a central role in career transitions, motivating their use in career path prediction (CPP) systems. In this work, we critically examine whether explicit skill representations provide complementary signal beyond text-based job representations. We evaluate multiple strategies for incorporating skills into CPP models, including score fusion and neural architectures, under two conditions: predicted skills and ground-truth ESCO annotations. Surprisingly, across two benchmark datasets, none of these settings yield substantial improvements over strong text-only baselines. Even when using ground-truth skills, gains remain marginal and inconsistent. Through detailed analysis, we identify key factors underlying this result: high redundancy between textual and skill representations, limited discriminative power of ESCO's taxonomy, and representational collapse in skill embeddings. translated_title: 当职业衍生技能无法发挥作用：论技能增强型职业路径预测的局限性
translated_abstract: 技能被广泛认为在职业转换中发挥着核心作用，这推动了技能在职业路径预测（CPP）系统中的应用。在这项工作中，我们批判性地考察了显式技能表示能否在基于文本的工作表示之外提供补充信号。我们在两种条件下——预测技能和真实（ground-truth）ESCO标注——评估了将技能融入CPP模型的多种策略，包括分数融合和神经架构。令人惊讶的是，在两个基准数据集上，这些设置均未比强大的纯文本基线带来实质性改进。即使使用真实技能标注，收益也依然微弱且不一致。通过详细分析，我们识别出导致这一结果的关键因素：文本表示与技能表示之间的高度冗余、ESCO分类体系有限的判别能力，以及技能嵌入中的表示坍缩。此外，我们发现技能…
tldr: 该研究批判性考察了技能表示在职业路径预测中的实际价值，发现无论是预测技能还是真实ESCO技能标注均无法显著超越纯文本基线，其根本原因在于文本与技能表示的高度冗余、ESCO分类判别力有限以及技能嵌入的表示坍缩。
en_tdlr: This study critically examines the value of skill representations in career path prediction, finding that neither predicted skills nor ground-truth ESCO annotations substantially outperform text-only baselines, due to high redundancy between textual and skill representations, the limited discriminative power of ESCO's taxonomy, and representational collapse in skill embeddings.
